findings.issue: create_before_destroy = true on hcloud_server.fabric and hcloud_volume_attachment.fabric_data is correct in isolation, but Hetzner does not permit a volume to be attached to two servers simultaneously. During a server replacement, Tofu will attempt to create the new attachment before destroying the old attachment. If Hetzner enforces single-server-per-volume, the new attachment creation will fail with a 409 conflict, leaving the replacement stuck. This is a provider-level constraint that create_before_destroy cannot work around.
findings.fix_recommendation: Add a comment to hcloud_volume_attachment.fabric_data lifecycle block noting this Hetzner single-attach constraint. In practice, during a server replace the old attachment is implicitly released when the old server is destroyed — but the ordering with create_before_destroy may trigger the conflict before that happens. Operators should be aware they may need to manually detach the volume before a server type change and reattach afterward if Tofu errors on the concurrent attach attempt.

findings.issue: The LOCKFILE REQUIREMENT comment correctly instructs the operator to commit .terraform.lock.hcl, but the lockfile is still absent from the repository. CI reproducibility is not yet achieved; it depends on the operator following through on the documented checklist step.
findings.fix_recommendation: Run `tofu -chdir=infrastructure/tofu/hetzner providers lock -platform=linux_amd64 -platform=darwin_amd64` and commit the resulting .terraform.lock.hcl before merging to main.

positive_notes: All three high-priority items from Round 1 are cleanly addressed: single merged lifecycle block with ignore_changes=[user_data,labels] and create_before_destroy=true, explicit SERVER TYPE CHANGE WARNING with operator checklist, and atomic firewall attachment via firewall_ids.
HCL2 single-lifecycle-block requirement is satisfied: one lifecycle block per resource throughout the file. No duplicate block syntax errors.
operator_ssh_pubkey validation in variables.tf is a meaningful security improvement: regex format check + 1024-char length guard prevents YAML injection via key rotation misuse.
PLAN_FILE=$(mktemp) with trap cleanup is correct and keeps CI workspaces clean. This was the right fix for the plan artifact leakage concern.

The egress-open/ingress-closed firewall design rationale comment (lines 38-41) correctly documents the layered security model: cloud firewall for L3, VM ufw/nftables for per-protocol egress hardening.
scope_observations: The automount partial finding is the only item where the recommended implementation diverged from the fix recommendation. The documentation-only approach adopted is defensible given that both values are true and the behaviour is correctly documented. The remaining not-addressed items (outputs.tf comment, root-level .gitignore) were explicitly advisory in Round 1 and remain acceptable deferrals. The new low finding on create_before_destroy + Hetzner single-attach constraint is a forward-looking risk note, not a blocking issue for the current bootstrap phase where the server has no live data.
